title: Put each parcel in the smallest compartment it fits
instruction: Move the four brown parcels from the blue mat on the left into the grey tray on the right, each into the smallest compartment it fits in, one parcel per compartment.
context: Mailroom and parcel-locker staff give each package the smallest compartment it fits, so the large ones stay free for large packages; dropping a small parcel into the nearest big slot leaves the next big parcel with nowhere to go. Done by: mail clerks, shipping and receiving clerks, postal and parcel-locker workers.
setup: All positions are of centres, measured from the line through the two arm bases: 'in front' is away from the arms, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, from the midline between the arms. A blue rubber delivery mat (28 cm front to back, 24 cm side to side, 3 mm thick) is fixed 26 cm in front and 29 cm left. Four brown cardboard parcels (closed boxes) stand on it: a medium parcel (6 x 6 cm, 6.5 cm tall, 250 g) 18 cm in front and 24 cm left; a large parcel (7 cm front to back, 11 cm side to side, 8.5 cm tall, 450 g) 33 cm in front and 24 cm left, its long side running side to side; two small parcels (4.5 x 4.5 cm, 6 cm tall, 100 g each) 18 and 32 cm in front, both 36 cm left. A green rubber handover mat (15 x 15 cm, 3 mm thick) is fixed on the midline 22 cm in front. A dark grey plastic sorting tray is fixed in front of the right arm: four open-top compartments in a row, each 8 cm front to back inside, centred 27 cm in front; 5 mm walls 3.4 cm tall stand around and between them on a 4 mm floor, so the rims are 3 cm above the compartment floors. From the midline outward the compartments are 12.5 cm wide (large, from 10 to 22.5 cm right), 7.5 cm (medium, 23 to 30.5 cm right), 5.5 cm (small, 31 to 36.5 cm right) and 5.5 cm (small, 37 to 42.5 cm right). Nothing else is on the table. The left arm cannot reach the tray and the right arm cannot reach the blue mat; both reach the green mat.
scoring: A parcel is in a compartment when its centre, seen from above, is inside that compartment's inner outline and either its bottom is less than 3 cm above the compartment floor (below the rim) or it rests on top of another parcel whose centre is inside the same outline (its bottom within 3 mm of that parcel's top, and moving under 1 cm/s). A parcel carried higher over the tray and not resting on another parcel is in no compartment. It is seated when, in addition, its bottom is within 5 mm of the compartment floor and one of its faces (any face: bottom, top or side) is tilted at most 10 degrees from horizontal. 0.25 for each parcel seated alone in a compartment of the smallest size it fits: a small parcel in either small compartment, the medium parcel in the medium compartment, the large parcel in the large compartment (on whichever face a parcel stands, these are the smallest it fits). A parcel in a compartment that holds another parcel (two parcels in one compartment as defined above, stacked or side by side) earns nothing. All four seated: 1.0. The score is 0 overall if any parcel is in a compartment larger than the smallest it fits (a small parcel in the medium or large compartment, or the medium parcel in the large one), or if any parcel has fallen off the table (its bottom more than 5 cm below the table top).
reset_notes: Lift the four parcels out and stand them back upright on their marks on the blue mat, the large parcel's long side running side to side; tape outlines on the mat make this quick. Which face a parcel stood on in the tray does not matter. The tray and both mats are taped or clamped down and do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: each parcel is one solid rigid box of uniform mass, not cardboard with contents, and nothing dents. The tray is fixed (clamp it down for real trials) and its walls stand only 3 cm above the compartment floors, lower than real cubbies, so the gripper's fingers clear them. Every object, the tray and mats included, has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than cardboard.
